curation.notes: src/lib.rs carries a safe and an unsafe twin per claim plus decoys: the unsafe twins are the discarded spawn statements (44, 45, and 380 after the test items), the long-lived async loops (66, 73; 213 whose await sits in a nested block; 238 with a timeout on each receive; 261 with a timeout_at deadline re-armed each round; 286 pacing on a moving sleep_until deadline; 321 polling with try_recv and a sleep), the three uncontracted unsafe blocks plus the uncontracted unsafe impl (106, 119, 125, 134) and the three unwrapped I/O entry points (139, 157, 171). The safe twins (stored/aborted handle, joined thread, awaited task, select! loop, shutdown-conditioned while, sync busy-collect loop, SAFETY-commented block and impl, with_timeout/deadline/builder-timeout calls) and every decoy (comment mentions, string literals, a SAFETY comment a blank line away from its block) must not fire. Neither may the loops that are not long-lived: a loop no .await drives (202, and the try_recv drain at 322), a loop run whole inside tokio::time::timeout (226), a while-let on a fixed timeout_at deadline (252), a loop that breaks once its deadline passes (273), and a try_recv drain in the shutdown arm of a select! (304). The file's own test items are test code and never claimed: the #[cfg(test)] mod inline_tests (336-360) and the file-level #[test] and #[tokio::test] fns (362-376) carry a would-be finding of every rule (342, 343, 344, 350, 352, 359, 364, 365, 372, 373). src/diagnostics.rs is reached only through #[cfg(test)] and carries a would-be finding of three rules: harness, never claimed.
